lines.trans: Good night, team! I refilled Rocio's two white jars for dawn!
Wait, Ernesto: those two white ceramic jars had little labels underneath!
Oh, the paper got wet when I wiped the counter, so I threw both labels away.
Tell me both jars held sugar, boss. Please tell me both were sugar.
No, one bag was fine white sugar and the other was fine sea salt!
Which jar got the sugar, Ernesto: the left one or the right one?!
The left! Definitely! ... Or did I turn both jars around when I wiped the lids?
If Clara puts four spoonfuls of salt in Wednesday's tarts, the inspector will run out!
Stay calm: tomorrow at six we taste a tiny pinch on a clean spoon before baking.
Write a big red note right now, Clara! Wait... who is knocking at the gate at ten?!
Look through the lobby glass: a woman in a blue coat with a city folder?!
Wait a moment: wasn't the inspector coming Wednesday at three, NOT Tuesday night?!

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.text: Vamos a la estación ahora.
examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Warm outer coat worn in cold or rainy weather.

examples.text: El abrigo está aquí.
examples.trans: The coat is here.

examples.text: Vemos los abrigos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the coats from the door.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization or understanding.

examples.text: ¡Ah, ya entiendo el mapa!
examples.trans: Ah, now I understand the map!

examples.text: ¿Ah, sí? Qué buena noticia.
examples.trans: Oh really? What good news.

meanings.note: Ahora mismo means 'right now'.

examples.text: Voy para allá ahora mismo.
examples.trans: I am heading there right now.

examples.text: Ahora tenemos cuatro mesas libres.
examples.trans: Now we have four free tables.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Feminine noun taking el in the singular before stressed a- (el alba, al alba).

examples.text: Rocío enciende el horno de la cocina al alba.
examples.trans: Rocio lights the kitchen oven at dawn.

examples.text: El patio huele a azahar fresco desde el alba.
examples.trans: The courtyard smells of fresh orange blossom from daybreak.

meanings.note: Antes de means 'before' a noun or infinitive.

examples.text: Llegué diez minutos antes.
examples.trans: I arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: Antes de salir, cierra la ventana.
examples.trans: Before leaving, close the window.

meanings.note: Así que means 'so / therefore'.

examples.text: Hazlo así, despacio.
examples.trans: Do it like this, slowly.

examples.text: Llueve mucho, así que entramos.
examples.trans: It is raining hard, so let us go inside.

meanings.note: Plural azules; azul marino means 'navy blue'.

examples.text: Tengo un coche azul.
examples.trans: I have a blue car.

examples.text: El cielo está muy azul hoy.
examples.trans: The sky is very blue today.

meanings.note: Commonly masculine (sin azúcar = without sugar).

examples.text: El azúcar es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The sugar is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el azúcar.
examples.trans: We talk about the sugar.

meanings.note: Quedarse blanco means 'to go pale'.

examples.text: Quiero una camisa blanca.
examples.trans: I want a white shirt.

examples.text: Las paredes del baño son blancas.
examples.trans: The bathroom walls are white.

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.text: ¡Buenos días a todos!
examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!

examples.text: Hace muy buen tiempo hoy.
examples.trans: The weather is very nice today.

meanings.note: Con calma means 'calmly / unhurriedly'.

examples.text: La calma es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The calm is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la calma.
examples.trans: We talk about the calm.

meanings.note: Document folder or stiff binder carried for inspections or checklists.

examples.text: Javier guarda los planos limpios en su carpeta azul.
examples.trans: Javier keeps the clean floor plans in his blue folder.

examples.text: Anota cada pedido de la mañana en esta carpeta.
examples.trans: Write down each morning order in this folder.

meanings.note: Refers both to the craft and to ceramic tableware.

examples.text: Compramos doce platos en el puesto de cerámica.
examples.trans: We bought twelve saucers at the pottery stall.

examples.text: La cerámica blanca queda preciosa sobre el mantel.
examples.trans: The white pottery looks lovely on the tablecloth.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.text: Tomo café con leche caliente.
examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.

examples.text: Habla con calma, por favor.
examples.trans: Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Entrar/salir corriendo = to run in / run out.

examples.text: Corro para no perder el tren.
examples.trans: I run so I do not miss the train.

examples.text: Los niños corrieron hacia la fuente.
examples.trans: The children ran toward the fountain.

meanings.note: Refers to window glass or crystal.

examples.text: Cuidado, el vaso es de cristal.
examples.trans: Careful, the glass is made of crystal.

examples.text: Limpio los cristales de las ventanas.
examples.trans: I'm cleaning the window panes.

meanings.note: Unaccented in statements and time clauses (interrogative: cuándo).

examples.text: Avísame cuando llegue el taxi.
examples.trans: Let me know when the taxi arrives.

examples.text: Cuando llueve, huele a tierra mojada.
examples.trans: When it rains, it smells like wet earth.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Tenemos cuatro mesas dentro.
examples.trans: We have four tables inside.

examples.text: La habitación cuatro da al patio.
examples.trans: Room four looks out onto the courtyard.

meanings.note: Table or soup spoon; cucharita is a teaspoon.

examples.text: Pon una cuchara limpia junto a cada cuenco.
examples.trans: Set a clean spoon beside each bowl.

examples.text: Prueba la sopa de lentejas con esta cuchara.
examples.trans: Taste the lentil soup with this spoon.

meanings.note: Built from cuchara ('spoon') + -ada.

examples.text: Pon una cucharada de miel dorada en el té.
examples.trans: Put a spoonful of golden honey in the tea.

examples.text: Añade dos cucharadas de azúcar a la masa.
examples.trans: Add two spoonfuls of sugar to the dough.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Debajo de + noun means 'underneath something'.

examples.text: Hay una llave pegada debajo.
examples.trans: There is a key taped underneath.

examples.text: Mira debajo de las ruedas.
examples.trans: Look underneath the wheels.

meanings.note: Querer decir means 'to mean'.

examples.text: ¿Qué dice la carta exactamente?
examples.trans: What does the letter say exactly?

examples.text: Dime la verdad sin miedo.
examples.trans: Tell me the truth without fear.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Soy vecino del barrio.
examples.trans: I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Opposite of izquierdo; el derecho means 'the right one'.

examples.text: El cajón derecho guarda las cucharas limpias de postre.
examples.trans: The right-hand drawer holds the clean dessert spoons.

examples.text: Mantén el cuadro bien derecho sobre la pared blanca.
examples.trans: Keep the picture nice and straight on the white wall.

meanings.note: Diez sobre diez = ten out of ten.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para empezar.
examples.trans: There are ten minutes left before starting.

examples.text: Su recepción merece un diez.
examples.trans: Your front desk deserves a ten.

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

echar.gloss: to pour; to toss; to miss (echar de menos)

meanings.en: to pour; to toss; to miss (echar de menos)
meanings.note: Echar un vistazo = take a glance; echar de menos = miss someone.

examples.text: Echa un poco más de agua caliente.
examples.trans: Pour a little more hot water.

examples.text: Te he echado mucho de menos.
examples.trans: I have missed you very much.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.text: El patio tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.

examples.text: Pásame el libro de reservas.
examples.trans: Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Standard Peninsular Spanish word for a kitchen countertop.

examples.text: Pasa un paño húmedo por toda la encimera de piedra.
examples.trans: Wipe a damp cloth across the whole stone worktop.

examples.text: Enharinamos la encimera limpia antes de estirar la masa.
examples.trans: We flour the clean counter before rolling out the pastry.

meanings.note: Doorway or entrance hall.

examples.text: Te espero en la entrada del museo.
examples.trans: I'll wait for you at the museum entrance.

examples.text: ¿Cuánto cuesta la entrada?
examples.trans: How much is the ticket?

meanings.note: Buen equipo = good team.

examples.text: El equipo está aquí.
examples.trans: The team is here.

examples.text: Vemos los equipos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the teams from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb with irregular past participle escrito.

examples.text: Escribo la nota con lápiz azul.
examples.trans: I write the note in blue pencil.

examples.text: Mi hermano me escribió una postal corta.
examples.trans: My brother wrote me a short postcard.

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.text: Pásame ese cuaderno azul.
examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

esperar.gloss: to wait; to wait for; to hope

meanings.en: to wait; to wait for; to hope
meanings.note: Covers both 'wait (for)' and 'hope'.

examples.text: Espere un momento, por favor.
examples.trans: Wait a moment, please.

examples.text: Esperamos que descanse muy bien.
examples.trans: We hope you rest very well.

meanings.note: Luggage tag or bottle label.

examples.text: La etiqueta está aquí.
examples.trans: The tag is here.

examples.text: Vemos las etiquetas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tags from the door.

meanings.note: Por favor literally means 'as a favour'.

examples.text: El favor está aquí.
examples.trans: The favour is here.

examples.text: Vemos los favores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the favours from the door.

meanings.note: Describes thin glass/fabric as well as fine quality.

examples.text: El cristal de estos vasos es demasiado fino para el té.
examples.trans: The glass of these cups is too thin for tea.

examples.text: Corta el limón en rodajas muy finas.
examples.trans: Cut the lemon into very thin slices.

meanings.note: Gira a la izquierda = turn left.

examples.text: Gira a la izquierda después del puente.
examples.trans: Turn left after the bridge.

examples.text: Giró la llave dos veces con cuidado.
examples.trans: She turned the key twice carefully.

grande.gloss: big; large; great (gran before sg noun)

meanings.en: big; large; great (gran before sg noun)
meanings.note: Shortens to gran before any singular noun (un gran libro, una gran idea).

examples.text: Tenemos una mesa grande en el patio.
examples.trans: We have a big table in the courtyard.

examples.text: Es una gran noticia para todos.
examples.trans: It is great news for everyone.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.

examples.text: Ya hemos preparado las habitaciones.
examples.trans: We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.text: Sigue recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.

examples.text: Nos quedamos hasta el viernes.
examples.trans: We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Built from horno (oven).

examples.text: La panadera hornea bizcochos cada viernes.
examples.trans: The baker bakes sponge cakes every Friday.

examples.text: Esta mañana horneamos pan crujiente.
examples.trans: This morning we baked crusty bread.

meanings.note: Feminine: la inspectora.

examples.text: El inspector está aquí.
examples.trans: The inspector is here.

examples.text: Vemos los inspectores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the inspectors from the door.

meanings.note: Feminine form of inspector.

examples.text: La inspectora revisó los planos y la salida al patio.
examples.trans: The inspector checked the plans and the courtyard exit.

examples.text: Ofrecimos un vaso de agua fresca a la inspectora.
examples.trans: We offered a glass of cool water to the inspector.

meanings.note: a la izquierda = on the left; la mano izquierda = the left hand.

examples.text: Me duele el pie izquierdo.
examples.trans: My left foot hurts.

examples.text: Escribe con la mano izquierda.
examples.trans: She writes with her left hand.

meanings.note: Feminine: la jefa.

examples.text: Mi jefe es muy simpático.
examples.trans: My boss is very nice.

examples.text: Hoy la jefa no está en la oficina.
examples.trans: The boss isn't in the office today.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.

examples.text: La habitación tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.text: Las ventanas dan al jardín.
examples.trans: The windows face the garden.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las ocho.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at eight.

limpiar.gloss: to clean; to polish; to wipe

meanings.en: to clean; to polish; to wipe
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Limpio el mostrador con un paño seco.
examples.trans: I wipe the counter with a dry cloth.

examples.text: Limpiamos los farolillos para la fiesta.
examples.trans: We polished the lanterns for the party.

meanings.note: Opposite of sucio (dirty).

examples.text: La habitación ya está limpia.
examples.trans: The room is already clean.

examples.text: Necesito una toalla limpia.
examples.trans: I need a clean towel.

llamar.gloss: to call; to ring; to be named (llamarse)

meanings.en: to call; to ring; to be named (llamarse)
meanings.note: ¿Cómo se llama? asks someone's name.

examples.text: Soy de aquí, mucho gusto.
examples.trans: I am from here, pleased to meet you.

examples.text: Alguien llamó por teléfono ayer.
examples.trans: Someone called by phone yesterday.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb; llenarse de means 'to fill up with'.

examples.text: El sol de la mañana llena toda la galería.
examples.trans: Morning sunlight fills the whole sunroom.

examples.text: Llenamos las jarras de cristal con agua fresca.
examples.trans: We fill the glass jugs with cool water.

llevar.gloss: to carry; to wear; to take; to spend (time)

meanings.en: to carry; to wear; to take; to spend (time)
meanings.note: Versatile verb for carrying items, wearing clothes/glasses, or duration.

examples.text: Llevo dos tazas calientes al jardín.
examples.trans: I carry two hot cups to the garden.

examples.text: Hoy lleva un abrigo gris oscuro.
examples.trans: Today he is wearing a dark grey coat.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.text: Los vecinos vienen a desayunar.
examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: In azul marino, invariable or agreeing depending on style.

examples.text: Es una pieza marina.
examples.trans: It is a marine piece.

examples.text: ¿Esa es la vieja maleta azul marino del taller del abuelo?
examples.trans: Is that the old dark-blue bag from Grandfather's workshop?

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el martes, los martes.

examples.text: El martes está aquí.
examples.trans: The Tuesday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los martes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Tuesdays from the door.

meanings.note: La mañana = the morning; mañana (without article) = tomorrow.

examples.text: Por la mañana servimos café caliente.
examples.trans: In the morning we serve hot coffee.

examples.text: ¡Hasta mañana a las ocho!
examples.trans: See you tomorrow at eight!

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: Agrees with the noun it describes.
In ahora mismo, meaning right now, mismo strengthens the time word ahora. Now comes from ahora; mismo supplies emphasis without agreeing with a person in this expression.

examples.text: Tenemos el mismo trabajo.
examples.trans: We have the same job.

examples.text: Ahora mismo estoy ocupada.
examples.trans: I am busy right now.

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el miércoles, los miércoles.

examples.text: El miércoles está aquí.
examples.trans: The Wednesday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los miércoles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Wednesdays from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: La lluvia moja los adoquines grises.
examples.trans: The rain wets the grey cobblestones.

examples.text: Perdón por mojar la entrada con el paraguas.
examples.trans: Sorry for wetting the entrance with my umbrella.

meanings.note: De momento = for now.

examples.text: Un momento, ahora vuelvo.
examples.trans: One moment, I'll be right back.

examples.text: En este momento no puedo hablar.
examples.trans: I can't talk right now.

meanings.note: Plural las mujeres.

examples.text: Una mujer con paraguas azul preguntó por el café.
examples.trans: A woman with a blue umbrella asked about the café.

examples.text: Dos mujeres del barrio leen juntas junto al piano.
examples.trans: Two women from the neighbourhood read together by the piano.

meanings.note: Plural municipales.

examples.text: Es una pieza municipal.
examples.trans: It is a municipal piece.

examples.text: Bien pensado, Clara. Javier lee normas municipales de edificios cada semana.
examples.trans: Smart thinking, Clara. Javier reads city building rules every single week.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.text: Hoy no llueve en Valencia.
examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

meanings.note: ¡Buenas noches! = Good evening / Good night; esta noche = tonight.

examples.text: La noche está aquí.
examples.trans: The night is here.

examples.text: Vemos las noches desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the nights from the door.

meanings.note: Covers jotted notes, musical notes, and review scores.

examples.text: La nota está aquí.
examples.trans: The note is here.

examples.text: Vemos las notas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the notes from the door.

meanings.note: Becomes u before words starting with o- or ho-.

examples.text: ¿Prefieres café o té caliente?
examples.trans: Do you prefer coffee or hot tea?

examples.text: ¿Abrimos hoy o esperamos a mañana?
examples.trans: Do we open today or wait until tomorrow?

meanings.note: Spanish never puts un/una before otro (otra taza = another cup; otra vez = again).

examples.text: ¿Quiere otra taza de café?
examples.trans: Would you like another cup of coffee?

examples.text: Míralo otra vez a la luz.
examples.trans: Look at it again in the light.

meanings.note: Plural los papeles.

examples.text: Necesito papel y un bolígrafo.
examples.trans: I need paper and a pen.

examples.text: Escribe tu nombre en este papel.
examples.trans: Write your name on this piece of paper.

meanings.note: Wrapped package or parcel.

examples.text: El paquete está aquí.
examples.trans: The parcel is here.

examples.text: Vemos los paquetes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the parcels from the door.

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

meanings.note: Hermano pequeño = younger brother; de pequeño = as a child.

examples.text: Tengo un piso pequeño.
examples.trans: I have a small flat.

examples.text: Mi hermana pequeña tiene diez años.
examples.trans: My little sister is ten.

meanings.note: Una pizca de sal is the standard cooking measure for a tiny pinch.

examples.text: Añade una pizca de sal fina a la masa dulce.
examples.trans: Add a pinch of fine salt to the sweet pastry.

examples.text: Probamos una pizca de crema con una cuchara limpia.
examples.trans: We taste a tiny dab of cream with a clean spoon.

poner.gloss: to put; to set; to become (ponerse + adj)

meanings.en: to put; to set; to become (ponerse + adj)
meanings.note: Irregular: pongo, pon, puse, puesto; ponerse nervioso = get nervous.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas limpias en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two clean cups on the table.

examples.text: Pon la maleta junto al mostrador.
examples.trans: Set the suitcase beside the counter.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.text: Paseamos por el casco antiguo.
examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Augmentative of puerta; drops the written accent in plural portones.

examples.text: Colgamos el cartel de madera junto al portón principal.
examples.trans: We hung the wooden sign beside the main front gate.

examples.text: El portón de la calle se cierra a las diez.
examples.trans: The street gate closes at ten o'clock.

probar.gloss: to try; to taste; to test

meanings.en: to try; to taste; to test
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: pruebo).

examples.text: Prueba este pan con aceite de oliva.
examples.trans: Try this bread with olive oil.

examples.text: Ayer probamos la mermelada de manzana.
examples.trans: Yesterday we tasted the apple jam.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.text: Espero que descanses muy bien.
examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

meanings.note: Plural quiénes; ¿de quién es? = whose is it?

examples.text: ¿Quién ha dejado este sobre aquí?
examples.trans: Who left this envelope here?

examples.text: ¿De quién es esta maleta azul?
examples.trans: Whose blue suitcase is this?

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.text: ¿Qué hora es ahora mismo?
examples.trans: What time is it right now?

examples.text: ¡Qué mañana tan luminosa!
examples.trans: What a bright morning!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number.

examples.text: Es una pieza roja.
examples.trans: It is a red piece.

examples.text: ¡Dígales que la mía tiene una cinta roja en el bolsillo de arriba!
examples.trans: Tell them mine has a red ribbon in the top pocket!

meanings.note: Con sal = salted; sin sal = unsalted.

examples.text: La sal es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The salt is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la sal.
examples.trans: We talk about the salt.

salir.gloss: to go out; to come out; to leave

meanings.en: to go out; to come out; to leave
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg salgo; salir corriendo = run out.

examples.text: El pan acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The bread just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Salgo temprano hacia la estación.
examples.trans: I leave early for the station.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.text: La puerta se abre despacio.
examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

meanings.note: Seguro que... = I bet / probably...

examples.text: ¿Estás seguro?
examples.trans: Are you sure?

examples.text: Este barrio es muy seguro.
examples.trans: This neighbourhood is very safe.

meanings.note: Las seis = six o'clock.

examples.text: Me despierto a las seis y media.
examples.trans: I wake up at six thirty.

examples.text: Tengo seis limones en la cesta.
examples.trans: I have six lemons in the basket.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.

examples.text: Esa maleta azul es mía.
examples.trans: That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Unaccented conjunction, distinct from accented sí ('yes').

examples.text: Avísame si necesitas otra manta.
examples.trans: Let me know if you need another blanket.

examples.text: Mira si queda leche en la nevera.
examples.trans: Check whether any milk is left in the fridge.

meanings.note: The lid of a box, pot or piano; in a Spanish bar also a small plate of food.

examples.text: ¿Dónde está la tapa de la olla?
examples.trans: Where is the lid of the pot?

examples.text: Pedimos una tapa de tortilla.
examples.trans: We order a small plate of tortilla.

meanings.note: Everyday word in Spain for a jam or honey jar.

examples.text: Guardamos la mermelada casera en tarros de cristal.
examples.trans: We keep the homemade jam in glass jars.

examples.text: Abre el tarro grande de miel con cuidado.
examples.trans: Open the big jar of honey carefully.

meanings.note: Usual word in Spain for a sweet tart or birthday cake.

examples.text: Hay tarta de chocolate para el postre.
examples.trans: There is chocolate cake for dessert.

examples.text: Mi abuela hace una tarta de manzana riquísima.
examples.trans: My grandmother makes a delicious apple tart.

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.text: Tenemos ocho habitaciones tranquilas.
examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: Tirar a la basura = throw in the bin.

examples.text: Tira el sobre viejo al contenedor azul.
examples.trans: Throw the old envelope into the blue recycling bin.

examples.text: Tiró suavemente del cordón de la campana.
examples.trans: She pulled the bell cord gently.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Ponemos tres mesas bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We set three tables under the tree.

examples.text: Empieza con tres frases cortas.
examples.trans: Start with three short sentences.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

venir.gloss: to come (el verano que viene = next summer)

meanings.en: to come (el verano que viene = next summer)
meanings.note: Irregular: vengo, vienes, viene, vine.

examples.text: Gracias por venir esta mañana.
examples.trans: Thank you for coming this morning.

examples.text: Nos vemos la semana que viene.
examples.trans: See you next week.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.

examples.text: Son las siete y cuarto.
examples.trans: It is quarter past seven.
